cards.title: Why is there a ½ on the parchi?
cards.body: Half tablets look odd, but they're common on Indian prescriptions. There's usually a good reason, and a right way to handle them.

cards.title: Getting the dose just right
cards.body: Sometimes the dose the doctor wants sits between the strengths available. Half a tablet gets closer to it.

cards.title: Starting low
cards.body: Doctors sometimes begin with a smaller dose and adjust based on how the person responds. A half tablet is one way to do that.

cards.title: Not every tablet can be split
cards.body: Some tablets are coated or made to release slowly. Splitting them can be a problem. Always ask the chemist first.

cards.title: Look for the score line
cards.body: A line across the tablet often means it's made to be split. Still, check with the pharmacist for your specific medicine.

cards.title: Split clean, store the other half
cards.body: A tablet cutter gives cleaner halves than a kitchen knife. Ask the pharmacist how to store the remaining half.

cards.title: Half doses, full attention
cards.body: Write ½ clearly on the strip or in reminders. And never turn a half into a full on your own.

takeaway: Half tablets help fine-tune doses, but always ask the pharmacist whether a tablet can be split and how.
share: Send this to the one who breaks tablets with their teeth. You know who.
